decisions.decision: Defer the unmet Phase 6 Exit 4 obligation until before Phase 10 beta acceptance.
decisions.authority:
I approve a Level 3 deferral of Phase 6 Exit 4—“Editing resource use improves beyond normal noise, with complete end-to-end cost accounted for”—for its existing bounded Entry/Exit scope, to a mandatory acceptance condition before the Phase 10 beta gate.

Record four accepted exits and one deferred, unmet obligation. Do not report 5/5 acceptance. Permit only the necessary sequencing exception for separately authorised later Core development. Preserve normal per-slice checks, comparison paths and all retirement conditions.

I accept the bounded sequencing exposure. I remain accountable for delivery through a named Phase 10 integration owner and for acceptance after independent review. Numerical budgets or improvement on another workload cannot discharge this obligation. If it remains unmet, beta acceptance is blocked.
decisions.exclusions: Preserve measurement rules, retained negative evidence and stopped directions. Authorise only the directly dependent Level 3 repository alignment. This decision accepts no performance result, closes no phase, opens no subsequent phase, authorises no product implementation or legacy removal, and changes no output or release status.

decisions.decision: Approve five bounded TrackTemplate technical meanings. Divide the nine Phase 9 criteria in the accepted gate into four Pending Phase 9A exits and six Pending Phase 9B exits. The two phases stay Not started.
decisions.authority:
As TrackTemplate project owner, I approve the bounded terminology needed for the Phase 9A/9B programme decision.

Approve these TrackTemplate technical meanings through the canonical terminology owner:

- chair — a railway support fitting represented by TrackTemplate that supports and locates a rail at a sleeper, timber or other applicable support. Its exact type, geometry, components and rail interface come from the accepted chair definition.
- chair component — one named part of a chair definition or chair assembly, such as a base/plinth, seat, jaw, rib, fillet, key, fastening or interface component.
- procedural chair geometry — derived chair geometry constructed deterministically from accepted "ChairDefinition" data and named chair components. It is not retained "Part" geometry, an opaque mesh or a hand-drawn final body.
- procedural chair generator — the TrackTemplate software path that constructs procedural chair geometry from an accepted "ChairDefinition".
- construct — create derived chair geometry from accepted canonical chair-definition data without changing that canonical data.

Do not approve constituent as a second project term where chair component expresses the required meaning.

Do not change the existing registered meaning of Regenerate. Do not use "Regenerate" for chair construction in the new Phase 9 planning prose.

This terminology decision does not resolve or accept:

- "ordinary chair";
- the precise S1 prototype designation;
- any particular chair-family classification;
- S1 dimensions, rail section, tolerances or constituent/component evidence;
- provenance, licence, rights or "project-cleared" status;
- production geometry or output acceptance.

Treat the previous Phase 9A/9B split candidate, its partial corrections and its BLOCKED Documentation Review receipt as retained failed-candidate evidence only. Do not resume, amend or re-review that candidate.

From clean protected "main", start one genuinely new reviewed Phase 9A/9B programme-alignment cycle using my existing direction:

Phase 9A proves the reusable procedural-chair architecture, centred on S1 with the smallest additional structurally distinct chair/support evidence needed to demonstrate that the architecture generalises.

Phase 9B uses the accepted Phase 9A architecture to complete all chair and support families required for the agreed TrackTemplate Core release candidate and to complete production-record, provenance, export and performance qualification.

Reallocate the existing nine Phase 9 requirements losslessly between 9A and 9B. Do not weaken, discard or invent requirements merely to make the split convenient.

Apply the normal candidate-bound documentation lifecycle to the new candidate.

If the new programme alignment is exact-green and independently accepted, integrate it through the normal protected-main workflow and open Phase 9A at 0/n.

Do not open Phase 9B.

Do not begin Phase 9A product implementation in this cycle.

Stop with clean, synchronised protected "main" and bring me the first bounded Phase 9A product recommendation.
decisions.exclusions: The previous BLOCKED candidate stays failed evidence only and gains no retrospective acceptance. Do not approve constituent as a second term or change Regenerate. Ordinary chair, S1 prototype designation and all listed evidence, rights, package and output questions stay open. No exit, product work, chair package, production output, risk closure, performance result, release, Phase 9B opening or legacy removal is accepted. Phase 9A opening requires separate exact-green integration after this alignment. Preserve D-P6-008 Deferred — unmet, TERM-R04 open, all 24 live risks and limits, private-development output, unknown project status and all legacy-retirement conditions.
